Here’s the full 12-week integrated plan summary for your 45-year-old client with type 2 diabetes on metformin (HbA1c 7.2), incorporating strength, cardio (including morning fasted sessions), intensified Phase 3, nutrition (with TRE option), weekly indulgence meal, and recovery/monitoring. It’s organized by phases and weeks with clear sessions, sets/reps, and key nutrition/timing notes.

Medical and safety notes
- Medical clearance recommended for progressive resistance and intervals.
- BG checkpoints: pre- and post-exercise during first 2–3 weeks and after any intensity change. Carry 15–20 g rapid carbs.
- Pre-exercise BG guide: <90 mg/dL take 10–15 g fast carb; 90–250 proceed; >250 with symptoms or >300 postpone intensity, hydrate.
- Foot care, hydration 2–3 L/day, electrolytes for longer/hot sessions.

Program structure
- Frequency: 4 main training days/week (2 strength, 2 cardio). Plus 3–5 short fasted morning cardio sessions (easy), and optional Sun walk/mobility.
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–4: Foundation and insulin sensitivity
  - Weeks 5–8: Progressive overload + metabolic conditioning
  - Weeks 9–12: Intensified strength and intervals (Phase 3 push)
- Weekly metrics: body weight, waist, step count, fasting BG, CGM time-in-range if available, sleep hours, training loads, RPE.

Standard warm-up and cool-down
- Warm-up: 5–8 min easy cardio + 5 min dynamic mobility + 1–2 ramp-up sets.
- Cool-down: 5 min easy cardio + 5–8 min stretching. If post-BG <90 or dropping, have 10–15 g carb.

Fasted morning cardio (added across all phases)
- Goal: 3–5 mornings/week, Zone 1–low Zone 2 (RPE 3–4), water/electrolytes allowed.
- Duration/progression:
  - Weeks 1–2: 20–25 min, 3x/week
  - Weeks 3–4: 25–30 min, 4x/week
  - Weeks 5–8: 30–35 min, 4–5x/week
  - Weeks 9–12: 35–40 min, 4–5x/week (or maintain 30–35 if recovery dips)
- On strength days keep ≤25–30 min; skip Sat fasted if doing intervals later fed.
- If waking BG <90 mg/dL, take 10–15 g fast carb or do a small protein-carb snack (safety over strict fasting).

Weekly schedule template
- Mon: AM fasted cardio; PM Strength A
- Tue: AM fasted cardio; PM Zone 2 cardio + core
- Thu: AM fasted cardio; PM Strength B
- Sat: Intervals (or Zone 2 early phase), fed
- Optional Sun: 30–45 min easy walk + mobility

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation)
Week 1
- Strength A
  - Goblet squat 3×10 (RPE 6–7)
  - Machine chest press 3×10
  - Lat pulldown 3×10
  - DB Romanian deadlift 3×10
  - Seated cable row 2×12
  - Pallof press 2×12/side
  - Farmer carry 2×40 m
- Cardio (Tue): Zone 2, 30 min
- Strength B
  - Leg press 3×12
  - DB incline press 3×10
  - Assisted split squat 3×8/side
  - Cable pull-through 3×12
  - Shoulder press machine 2×12
  - Dead bug 2×10/side
  - Sled push (light) 2×20 m
- Cardio (Sat): Zone 2, 30 min + core (plank 2×30–45 s, side plank 2×20–30 s/side)

Week 2
- Progress load +2.5–5% where RPE ≤7 or add a set to first upper/lower move.
- Cardio: 32–35 min Zone 2 both days.
- Add glute bridge 2×12 to Strength B.

Week 3
- Strength A
  - Box squat or goblet squat 4×8
  - Chest press 4×8
  - Lat pulldown 3×10
  - DB RDL 3×10
  - Face pull 3×12
  - Pallof press 3×10/side
- Cardio: 35–38 min Zone 2
- Strength B
  - Leg press 4×10
  - DB incline press 3×10
  - Split squat 3×8/side
  - Hip thrust 3×10 (light–moderate)
  - Seated row 3×10
  - Anti-rotation walkouts 2×10/side

Week 4 (deload-light build)
- Keep exercises; RPE 6–7; maintain volume.
- Cardio: 38–40 min Zone 2; add 3×20 s brisk pick-ups with 60 s easy.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Progressive overload + intervals intro)
Week 5
- Strength A (heavier)
  - Back squat or goblet 4×6–8 (RPE 7–8)
  - Barbell/machine bench 4×6–8
  - Romanian deadlift 3×8
  - Lat pulldown 3×8–10
  - DB walking lunge 2×10/side
  - Cable curl + triceps pressdown 2×12 each
- Cardio: Tue 40 min Zone 2; Sat intervals intro 6×30 s fast/90 s easy (10 min WU/CD)

Week 6

  - Leg press 4×8–10
  - DB incline press 4×8
  - Hip thrust 4×8
  - Seated row 3×8–10
  - Split squat 3×8/side
  - Face pull 2×15
- Cardio: Tue 42 min Zone 2; Sat 7×30 s fast/90 s easy

Week 7

  - Squat 4×6–8 (add 2.5–5% if W5 easy)
  - Bench press 4×6–8
  - RDL 3×8
  - Pull-down 3×8–10
  - Step-up 3×10/side
  - Farmer carry 3×30–40 m
- Cardio: Tue 45 min Zone 2; Sat 8×30 s/90 s

Week 8 (volume consolidation)
- Keep lifts; add 1 set to accessories or hold load and perfect form.
- Cardio: Tue 45–48 min Zone 2; Sat 6×45 s/2 min easy.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Intensity push)
Week 9
- Strength A (heavy 5s + EMOM finisher)
  - Back squat 5×5 (RPE 7–8, 2–3 min rest)
  - Bench press 5×5 (RPE 7–8)
  - Romanian deadlift 4×6 (RPE 7)
  - Lat pulldown 3×8–10
  - Finisher EMOM 8 min: KB swing 12–15 / Air bike 55–65 s moderate (alternate minutes)
- Strength B (strength + power)
  - Trap-bar deadlift 4×4–5 (RPE 7–8)
  - Incline DB press 4×6–8
  - Hip thrust 4×6–8 (1 s pause)
  - Seated row 3×8–10
  - Split squat 3×8/side
  - Power: Med-ball chest pass 3×6
- Intervals (Sat, fed)
  - 10 min warm-up
  - 6×60 s hard (Z4) / 2.5–3 min easy
  - 8–10 min cool-down
- Tue: Zone 2, 45–50 min

Week 10
- Strength A (slightly heavier)
  - Back squat 5×4–5 @ RPE 8
  - Bench press 5×4–5 @ RPE 8
  - RDL 4×5–6 @ RPE 7–8
  - Chest-supported row 3×8–10
  - Finisher EMOM 8–9 min: 10 cal air bike (hard but controlled) + 8 KB swings
- Strength B
  - Trap-bar deadlift 5×3–4 @ RPE 8
  - Incline press 4×6–8
  - Hip thrust 4×6–8 (tempo 3–1–1 or load up)
  - Pull-ups/assisted 3×6–8 or Lat pulldown 3×8
  - Reverse lunge 3×8/side
  - Power: KB high pull or light push press 3×5 (RPE 6–7)
- Intervals: 7×60 s hard / 2.5–3 min easy
- Tue: Zone 2, 50–55 min

Week 11 (peak)
- Strength A
  - Back squat 4×3–4 @ RPE 8–9 (no failures)
  - Bench press 4×3–4 @ RPE 8–9
  - RDL 3×5 @ RPE 8
  - 1-arm DB row 3×8/side
  - Finisher (10 min cap): Every 2 min ×5 rounds: 10 KB swings + 8 step-back lunges/side
- Strength B
  - Trap-bar deadlift 5×3 @ RPE 8–9 (cut set if bar speed drops)
  - Incline press 4×5–6
  - Hip thrust 4×5–6 (heaviest)
  - Seated row 3×8
  - Bulgarian split squat 3×8/side
  - Power: Med-ball slam 3×6
- Intervals (peak)
  - 5×90 s hard (upper Z4/low Z5) / 3 min easy
  - Alt: 8×45 s hard / 2 min easy if HR too high
- Tue: Zone 2, 50–55 min (or 45 if fatigue high)

Week 12 (taper/test)
- Strength A
  - Back squat 3×3 @ RPE 8
  - Bench press 3×3 @ RPE 8
  - RDL 2×5 @ RPE 7
  - Pull-down 2×8
  - Optional finisher: 6 min easy EMOM swings 10 + bike 8 cal
- Strength B
  - Trap-bar deadlift 3×3 @ RPE 7–8
  - Incline press 3×5
  - Hip thrust 2×5
  - Row 2×8
  - Mobility/core 10–12 min
- Intervals
  - If fresh: 4×90 s hard / 3 min easy; otherwise Zone 2 40–45 min.
- Reassess: waist, body weight, 5RM estimates from RPE 8 sets, average fasting BG, time-in-range.

Step targets and post-meal walks
- Weeks 1–2: 6,500–7,500 steps/day
- Weeks 3–4: 7,500–8,500
- Weeks 5–8: 8,500–9,500
- Weeks 9–12: 9,500–10,500
- Add 10–15 min walks after larger-carb meals to blunt spikes.

Nutrition (fat loss + glycaemic control)
- Calories: Start ~25–30% below maintenance (or 10–12 kcal/lb body weight). Adjust −100 to −150 kcal if weight loss <0.3–0.7%/wk for 2 weeks.
- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g/lb goal body weight (or 0.8–1.0 g/lb current), split across 3–4 meals.
- Carbs: 30–40% calories (approx. 90–160 g/day depending on total kcal). Distribute evenly: 25–40 g net carbs per meal; pair with protein/fiber; focus on low-GI, high-fiber sources.
- Fat: Remainder of calories; keep saturated fat <10% of calories.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day.
- Carb quality: legumes, berries, apples/citrus, oats/steel-cut oats, quinoa, barley, wholegrain sourdough, sweet potato in moderate portions, lots of non-starchy veg. Limit refined grains, sweets, sugary drinks.
- Pre-workout (strength/interval days, 60–120 min prior): 25–35 g protein + 25–40 g low‑GI carbs.
- Post-workout: 25–35 g protein + 20–40 g carbs depending on post-BG.
- Fasted cardio days pre: optional light mini-breakfast if BG <90–100 or she feels better fed (15–25 g protein + 10–25 g low‑GI carbs, ≤200 kcal). Otherwise water/electrolytes only.
- Post fasted cardio snack ideas: Greek yogurt + berries; RTD protein shake + small fruit; cottage cheese + Wasa cracker (adjust carbs to BG).

- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g per lb of goal body weight (or 0.8–1.0 g/lb current if goal not set), spread across 3–4 meals. Supports satiety, lean mass retention, and glycaemic control.
- Carbohydrate: moderate, distributed, mostly low‑GI/high‑fiber.

- Start meals with non‑starchy veg and protein; finish starches last.

- Pair carbs with protein/fat/fiber; avoid naked carbs.
- If using a CGM, test individual responses to oats, rice, potatoes, and adjust portions/choices.

- For the first 2 weeks and after any interval progression:
  - Check pre‑session BG.
  - If pre‑strength 90–140 mg/dL and she historically drops, consider 10–15 g carb pre or intra (e.g., a small apple).

- Keep consistent meal timing day to day to stabilize glycaemia.

Intermittent fasting (IF) can be compatible with type 2 diabetes and fat loss, but it should be implemented conservatively, monitored with BG checks, and adjusted for training quality. For a 45-year-old on metformin, the safest, most sustainable option is time-restricted eating (TRE) with an earlier eating window.

Key considerations (diabetes-specific)
- Safety first: Metformin alone has low hypoglycaemia risk, but exercise + long gaps between meals can drop BG. Monitor fasting, mid‑window, and post‑exercise BG during the first 2 weeks and after any change.
- Medication timing: Keep metformin at its prescribed times with meals (usually breakfast/dinner). If shifting meal timing, clear any med-time changes with her clinician.
- Training quality: Strength days need adequate fuel. If IF degrades performance, shorten the fasting window or place main meals around training.
- Sleep and stress: Long evening fasts can improve sleep for some; skipping breakfast can worsen appetite for others. Choose the pattern that controls hunger and preserves adherence.

Recommended approach: Early time-restricted eating (eTRE)
- Structure: 10-hour eating window, 14-hour fast, 5–6 days per week.
  - Example: 8:00–18:00 window (or 9:00–19:00 if schedule requires).
  - Meals: 3 meals + optional small protein/fiber snack if needed.
- Why early? Front-loading calories earlier and finishing dinner 2–3 hours before bed can improve insulin sensitivity, postprandial glucose, sleep, and GERD risk.
- Progression:
  - Weeks 1–2: 12-hour window (e.g., 8:00–20:00) to test tolerance.
  - Weeks 3–12: Move to 10-hour window (e.g., 8:00–18:00). Use 1–2 flexible days per week (social/travel) where the window extends to 12 hours.

How to integrate with her 12-week program
- Fasted morning cardio: Keep as planned at low intensity. If waking BG <90 mg/dL or she feels shaky, take 10–15 g carb (breaks the fast, but safety first).
- Strength sessions (Mon/Thu) and intervals (Sat):
  - Place a protein‑carb meal 60–120 min pre‑workout within the eating window.
  - Post-workout: have 25–35 g protein + 20–40 g low‑GI carbs within the window.
  - If she must lift late and it pushes dinner late, either shift training earlier or allow the window to extend on those days.
- Weekly indulgence meal: Schedule inside the eating window, ideally after training. Keep the same guardrails (protein first, walk after, cap calories).

Calorie and macro guidance during IF
- Keep the same daily calorie and macro targets as prescribed. IF is a meal‑timing tool, not a license to undereat protein or back‑load huge high‑fat/high‑sugar dinners.
- Protein: 25–35 g at each of 3 meals (aim for 90–120 g/day depending on her target).
- Carbs: Evenly divide her daily carbs across meals to limit spikes (e.g., 25–40 g net carbs per meal), with most around training.
- Hydration/electrolytes during the fast: water, black coffee/tea, zero‑calorie electrolytes. Non‑nutritive sweeteners are generally fine if they don’t trigger cravings.

Sample eTRE day (10-hour window: 8:00–18:00)
- 06:30: Fasted easy walk (20–30 min). If BG <90, take 10–15 g carb.
- 08:00 (Meal 1): Omelet (2 eggs + 2 whites) + spinach/mushrooms + 1 slice wholegrain; berries; coffee.
- 12:30 (Meal 2): Turkey quinoa bowl: 4–5 oz turkey, 1/2 cup quinoa, big salad, olive oil/lemon.
- 16:30 (Strength session)
- 17:45 (Meal 3, post-workout): Skyr bowl (6–7 oz) + 1/2 cup berries + chia; plus salmon 4–5 oz + roasted veg. Finish eating by 18:00.
- 20:30: Herbal tea; no calories.

Monitoring and adjustments
- Track: fasting BG, 2‑hr postprandials (especially when changing the window), energy, hunger, training performance, and sleep.
- If morning BG rises (dawn phenomenon) or post‑meal spikes worsen:
  - Shift more calories to breakfast/lunch, reduce dinner carbs, and/or move the window earlier.
- If strength performance suffers or she’s excessively hungry:
  - Widen to a 12-hour window on training days or add a small protein snack (100–150 kcal) pre‑session even if it breaks the fast—performance and adherence beat strict fasting.
- If weight loss stalls for 2+ weeks despite compliance:
  - Reassess calorie intake, step count, and sleep before tightening the window further. Consider a slight calorie reduction (−100–150 kcal/day) or an extra 10–15 min of low‑intensity walking on 2 days.

Who should avoid aggressive IF
- History of disordered eating, significant gastroparesis, recurrent nocturnal hypoglycaemia, or if on insulin/sulfonylureas without medical supervision.

Bottom line
- Use a gentle 10-hour early eating window most days, keep protein and fiber high, place carbs around training, and prioritize BG stability over strict fasting rules. Adjust the window pragmatically to protect training quality and long-term adherence.
